Physical supply chain: 1. Raw materials: quartz, copper, specialty minerals and gases
Economic relationships: Mining, refining, commodity sales and supply contracts
Geographic concentration: China: mineral processing. Australia, Chile and U.S.: key raw materials.

Physical supply chain: 2. Semiconductor materials: silicon, wafers, photoresists and chemicals
Economic relationships: Purification, specialty processing and supplier qualification
Geographic concentration: Japan: wafers and photoresists. U.S., Germany and South Korea: chemicals and gases.

Physical supply chain: 3. Chip design and EDA: architecture, circuit design and verification
Economic relationships: R&D, software licensing and intellectual property
Geographic concentration: U.S.: NVIDIA, AMD, Broadcom, Synopsys and Cadence.

Physical supply chain: 4. Manufacturing equipment: lithography, etching, deposition and inspection
Economic relationships: Equipment sales, maintenance and supplier contracts
Geographic concentration: Netherlands: ASML. U.S.: Applied Materials, Lam Research and KLA. Japan: Tokyo Electron.

Economic relationships: Foundry contracts, capital investment and yield improvement
Geographic concentration: Taiwan: TSMC. South Korea: Samsung. U.S.: Intel and TSMC Arizona. China: SMIC. Capabilities differ.

Physical supply chain: 6. Memory and packaging: HBM, chiplets and advanced packaging
Economic relationships: Memory sales, packaging services and capacity reservations
Geographic concentration: South Korea: SK hynix and Samsung. U.S.: Micron. Taiwan: TSMC packaging.

Physical supply chain: 7. Servers and networking: accelerators, CPUs, switches, storage and racks
Economic relationships: Hardware sales, system integration and networking equipment
Geographic concentration: U.S.: NVIDIA and Broadcom. Taiwan: Quanta, Wiwynn and Foxconn.

Physical supply chain: 8. Data centers and compute: GPU clusters, power, cooling and connectivity
Economic relationships: Cloud rentals, infrastructure investment and power purchases
Geographic concentration: U.S.-based AWS, Azure and Google Cloud. Power and permitting constraints vary locally.

Physical supply chain: 9. Foundation models: pretraining, post-training and inference
Economic relationships: Compute spending, API fees, subscriptions and enterprise contracts
Geographic concentration: U.S.: OpenAI, Anthropic, Google and Meta. China: DeepSeek and Alibaba.

Physical supply chain: 10. AI applications: agents, enterprise tools and consumer products
Economic relationships: Subscriptions, API fees, licensing and workflow integration
Geographic concentration: Global developers, often reliant on model providers and infrastructure.

Physical supply chain: 11. End users: governments, businesses and consumers
Economic relationships: Customer spending, adoption and potential productivity gains
Geographic concentration: Global demand, shaped by regulation, procurement and data rules.
